If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to offset bearish pressure.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal risk.

If sentiment remains neutral (0.33–0.67) across 5+ days, apply a 0.5–1.0% downward bias in late horizon (16–30 days) to account for mean reversion.

If sentiment peaks >0.80 in last 3 days and forecast is below 70, add 1–2% upward bias in mid-horizon to capture sentiment-driven breakout potential.

If sentiment is negative but price is trending upward (true > forecast), reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon to avoid overcorrection from momentum.
